unresolved_assumptions_and_questions: ASM-001 constrains DEC-011 because both endpoints keep the engine-neutral component design visibly non-authoritative until OQ-008 is answered.

ASM-001: ASSUMPTION: A framework-neutral component design can preserve the gameplay intent until the engine and programming language are selected; this is non-authoritative and may change after OQ-008 is answered.
ASM-002 constrains DEC-008 because both endpoints treat the single logical room as a non-authoritative implementation inference.

ASM-002: ASSUMPTION: A single logical room can contain the station, callers, routes, hazards, and approaching entities needed to exercise the full loop; this is non-authoritative and must be tested against REQ-005.
ASM-003 constrains DEC-006 because both endpoints label 300 seconds as the inferred nominal centre and not the duration tolerance.
ASM-003: ASSUMPTION: The nominal centre of “about five minutes” is 300 seconds; this is non-authoritative and does not define the unresolved duration tolerance in OQ-005.
ASM-004 constrains DEC-012 because both endpoints label deterministic simulation fixtures as engine-neutral but non-authoritative.

ASM-004: ASSUMPTION: Deterministic simulation fixtures and event logs are feasible for tuning, entities, rescue state, and scoring regardless of the eventual engine; this is non-authoritative and may change after OQ-008 is answered.
ASM-005 constrains the telemetry portion of TechnicalArchitecture.md because both endpoints keep non-identifying metrics provisional pending OQ-009.

ASM-005: ASSUMPTION: Playtest instrumentation may collect run duration, rescues, signal error, dangerous-band exposure, deaths or failures, and post-run responses without collecting direct personal identifiers; this is non-authoritative pending a telemetry and consent decision.

Colour roles are provisional. No gameplay meaning may rely on this palette as a settled accessibility solution; candidate redundant shape, motion, text, or pattern channels remain subject to OQ-001 and DEC-013.

If sound carries gameplay-critical information before OQ-001 is resolved, the first playable may embody an unapproved accessibility choice; DEC-010 prevents that choice from being mislabeled as settled.

Layer dry radio clicks, narrow-band voice texture, wind pressure, carrier tones, and hostile interference so tuning feels physical. Gameplay must not assume any no-audio equivalent until OQ-001 is answered; sound-layering here implements the permitted material in CON-001, not accessibility scope.
Non-authoritative inference under ASM-004: deterministic scenarios could make frequency reveals, hearing transitions, rescue timing, and score components cheap to regression-test.
Non-authoritative inference under ASM-005: collecting playtest telemetry without an answer to OQ-009 could create privacy and consent obligations not covered by this package.
OQ-001: Which, if any, deaf or hard-of-hearing support features belong in the first playable, and which defaults and parity rules are stakeholder-approved?
OQ-002: What relative scoring weights or incentive hierarchy should govern rescues, signal accuracy, and risky time near dangerous bands?
OQ-003: What measurable player-experience boundary distinguishes intriguing hidden information from unfair hidden information?
OQ-004: Who is the intended audience for Dead Air Dispatch, or is audience discovery authorized?
OQ-005: What permitted deviation defines “about five minutes” for run duration?
OQ-006: What observed results justify continuing, revising, or stopping after the first playable?
OQ-007: What project-specific work is explicitly excluded from the first playable and later product?
OQ-008: Which engine, language, renderer, audio stack, packaging toolchain, and minimum supported PC configuration are approved?
OQ-009: What telemetry, consent, retention, and privacy boundaries apply to playtests?
Preserved all seven supplied ANS records verbatim and kept their corresponding questions open; added OQ-008 and OQ-009 for technology and telemetry choices exposed by the package.
Score priorities are not defined, so the displayed total cannot yet communicate a stakeholder-approved incentive hierarchy; see OQ-002.

Seeded scenarios expose known reveal bands, hearing bands, caller hold times, and approach paths. A virtual clock permits exact 300-second target inspection without waiting in real time. The ordered event log supports the reveal, entity, loop, duration, and scoring acceptance checks. Any telemetry implementation remains blocked by OQ-009.

TechnicalArchitecture.md uses an engine-neutral component model under ASM-001 and ASM-004. That model is a reversible design inference, not proof that any engine satisfies the project. OQ-008 must be answered before tool-specific interfaces, build targets, performance budgets, or license obligations become settled.

The canonical product requirements above derive from the brief, not from the imported auto-generated “clarified project choice” candidates. The seven ANS records preserve why those candidates do not settle stakeholder-owned choices. “About five minutes” is represented as a 300-second nominal target; the acceptable deviation remains OQ-005.

The domain layer owns the tuner, frequency field, caller state, entity hearing and approach, antenna threat, run clock, and score ledger. Adapters translate mouse-wheel input, 2D visuals, static and waveform effects, layered sound, local save data, and platform packaging. This separation keeps the design usable before OQ-008 selects technology.

The first playable should make every brief-derived gameplay record observable and collect only the measurements authorized after OQ-003, OQ-006, and OQ-009 are answered. It is not yet authorized to claim audience fit, accessibility completeness, a fair hidden-information threshold, or project success.

`ITuningInput`, `IClock`, `IRandomSource`, and `IScenarioLoader` must be injectable. `IPresentation`, `IAudioOutput`, `IAccessibilityOutput`, `IMetricsSink`, and `ISaveStore` are adapters. `IAccessibilityOutput` is an empty extension seam until OQ-001 is answered; its existence does not settle a feature.
`RunMetrics`: nominal target, actual duration, ordered events, failures, and optional non-identifying playtest responses under ASM-005.
